item.title: AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale gives Ruben Amorim unconditional backing and insists Scudetto is '100% possible'
item.description: AC Milan v Atalanta BC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport RedBird Capital chief Gerry Cardinale has broken his silence on the current state of AC Milan, offering a ringing endorsement of manager Ruben Amorim. Despite a turbulent start to the campaign, the American owner remains convinced that the foundations for long-term success are firmly in place at San Siro. Cardinale clarifies stance on Ruben Amorim The hierarchy at Milan has moved to dispel any rumors regarding the job security of Amorim, with owner Cardinale offering his full support to the Portuguese tactician. Following a summer of significant change, the Rossoneri have experienced a mixed run of form that led to external questions about the direction of the project. However, Cardinale has stepped in to ensure that the internal belief in Amorim’s methods remains as high as it was on the day he was appointed to lead the club into a new era. Speaking candidly about the managerial situation, the RedBird founder emphasized that the club is not looking for short-term fixes but rather a sustainable path to the top of European football. "I have full faith in him. At the end of Top Gun, 'my' film, there's a great line: 'I'm not leaving my wingman', Tom Cruise says. And I'm not leaving Ruben. He is in no danger whatsoever. I will stand by his side. I won't make the mistakes made in recent years. He is my manager and we'll keep working together until we manage to make the step up.,” Cardinale told La Gazzetta dello Sport . Scudetto remains the primary objective Despite currently trailing the pace-setters in the Serie A standings, Cardinale is refusing to temper his expectations for the current season. The American businessman dismissed suggestions that this might be a transition year for the club, instead doubling down on the ambition to bring the league title back to the red and black side of Milan. He views the competitive nature of the league as an opportunity rather than a hurdle, believing the squad is deep enough to compete. "It is entirely possible, 100%. And I say that without wanting to sound arrogant. I wake up every morning hoping for a small opening, meaning Inter start drawing instead of winning and we start stringing together a run of wins. Winning is the only thing that matters to me, but let's take it one match at a time, gaining ground on those ahead of us, matchday by matchday,” Cardinale stated firmly. item.title: 'Some of the things hurt me': Zimbabwe captain slams players' 'complacency' after series loss as Afghanistan go from 5 for 4 to score 221
item.description: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called "complacency" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat to Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The loss also handed Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Raza said his biggest concern was the attitude of some players after Zimbabwe had reduced Afghanistan to 5 for 4 in the fourth over. He felt the team had taken the opposition lightly at that stage, assuming Afghanistan would struggle to post a big total. "For me, before I go too much in detail [about the match] - and I will address that in the changing room - the toughest part to swallow was the complacency that I saw from some of the boys," Raza said after the match. The Zimbabwe captain was particularly unhappy that some players appeared to believe Afghanistan would manage only 130 or 140 runs after losing four wickets early. He said the team needed to stay focused and remember that a match is not over until the final ball. "[At 5 for 4] some of the boys were probably calculating that it will be - 130, 140 max - at the end of 20 overs. Some of the things that I saw on the ground today certainly hurt me and I'll address that in the changing room because, listen, it can happen but I think that's where you have to be mentally very strong and say, 'no, the game is never over until it's over - we still have a job in hand and I'm going to be the guy who's going to get the job done'. "Before I dissect the game with batting or bowling, I think that's something that I felt today out there in the middle and that's something that needs to be addressed, not to take this game for granted because it can bite back and today is a great example." Zimbabwe had also kept Afghanistan to 45 for 5 at the halfway stage of the innings. However, Azmatullah Omarzai's 116 off 50 balls and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai's 52 off 27 deliveries helped Afghanistan recover and post 221 for 7. Raza then led Zimbabwe's fightback with an unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, but his effort was not enough to prevent defeat. He said he had tried to keep his emotions under control while batting after being unhappy with the team's approach in the first innings. "When you're chasing 222, for me the biggest thing was to try and stay in control of my emotions because the way we conducted ourselves in the first innings hurt me," Raza said. "So when we go out to bat, for me it was trying to win the game from any position. That has been our motto and in my head, I was just calculating how best can I go about my business and hopefully the other batters chip in so that we can win the game. "Up until the last two overs [by when they needed 46 from 12], we were backing ourselves to win the game but yeah, I think we left ourselves too much." Raza also said he would address the issue with his teammates in the dressing room, making it clear that his message would be stronger than what he had said publicly. 135358996

item.title: Ohio State gets another shot at flipping top running back target
item.description: It’s been an interesting recruiting cycle for Ohio State at the running back position, and with the 2027 class still without a commitment at the spot, the Buckeyes are continuing to work toward changing that. Carlos Locklyn and the staff have certainly put in the effort, but the results haven’t gone their way to this point. After seeing top target David Gabriel-Georges choose Tennessee, Ohio State was dealt another tough blow last week when in-state prospect Jordan Hall committed to Penn State. With two of their top options now off the board, it’s fair to wonder where Ohio State turns next. The transfer portal remains an option, and many have assumed that’s the direction the Buckeyes will ultimately take. However, the coaching staff isn’t ready to throw in the towel on the high school recruiting trail just yet, and Thursday brought some encouraging news regarding a familiar name. Per Rivals, Gainesville, Georgia running back Nigel Newkirk has officially scheduled a visit to Columbus for Nov. 7, when Ohio State hosts Oregon. The Alabama commit has been on the Buckeyes’ radar for quite some time, and while his pledge to the Crimson Tide back in May appeared to put an end to Ohio State’s pursuit, Locklyn and the staff have continued to maintain contact. Clearly, that persistence is beginning to pay off. Getting Newkirk back on campus is a significant development for Ohio State, especially considering where things currently stand at the position. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound back is the No. 226 player nationally and the No. 16 running back in the 2027 class according to the 247Sports Composite rankings, and would be a major addition to a class that could certainly use some good news at running back. Of course, getting a committed prospect to visit and actually convincing him to flip are two very different things. Alabama won’t be eager to let Newkirk go, and Ohio State will still have plenty of work to do if it hopes to change his mind. Still, the opportunity to get him on campus for a marquee Big Ten matchup is about as good of a setting as the staff could ask for. The Buckeyes have had their share of frustrations recruiting running backs in this cycle, but they’re proving that they aren’t done fighting for the talent they want. Locklyn and company now have a legitimate opportunity to make up some ground, and the next step will be making sure Newkirk leaves Columbus with plenty to think about. item.title: Hansi Flick talks signing a new center-back and Barcelona’s defensive problems
item.description: Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images | Europa Press via Getty Images Barcelona’s defensive issues came into focus in their high-profile losses to PSG and Real Madrid last week, and talks of a new center-back signing have already started as we approach the January transfer window. Reports from Spanish media in the last 24 hours universally agree that Hansi Flick wants a new addition at the back this winter, and the coach pretty much confirmed that in a press conference on Friday. Flick also explained the root of the defensive issues in El Clásico , and focused on the importance of keeping the ball well and pressing from the front in addition to winning duels at the back. “I said it during the transfer window, we always talk about what’s best for the team, how we can improve it. It’s something we’re working on. We’ll see. We have a few weeks left before the transfer window opens. We’ve discussed it with Deco, Bojan, and my staff. That’s how we do things. If we can, maybe we will. “Ultimately, defending isn’t just the defenders’ job; even the striker defends. Everyone is involved. To begin with, we can’t lose the ball easily. We lost possession a few times against Real Madrid, which isn’t good. It’s something that happens to us often, and we need to play more intelligently, more focused. “When we’re defending in our own area, it’s also important to mark our opponents well, and we didn’t do that either. We have to improve in these situations. We train it, we take it into account, and we talk about it with the players.” I’ll believe it when I see it regarding the signing of a world-class center-back, something Barça have lacked since Iñigo Martínez left. But it’s at least good to see the clear intention from Flick and Deco to solve a pretty glaring issue when it comes to Barça’s ability to win the biggest games.

item.title: What did you think of the World Series?
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Cooper Pratt #12 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with the Commissioner's Trophy during the trophy presentation alongside teammates after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to win in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The World Series is over, and we’ve all had a day to sit with the result. The Milwaukee Brewers have been crowned champions for the first time in their history, and they did it through a very impressive run through the postseason after being the best team in the regular season. It may have appeared a fait accompli to some, as anyone closely watching this Brewers team could tell they were a juggernaut. But sometimes it’s entertaining to watch a great team simply be great, proving over and over again that they are indeed the best team in baseball for a given year. This World Series may not have been the seven game thriller last year’s series was, but it still had some great moments. The highlights of course being Milwaukee’s legendary eight run rally with two outs in the fifth inning of Game 3 and the Rays’ walk-off win to cap off a 12-inning epic. Nevertheless, it would be fair to feel a little disappointed with how quickly the series ended after all the hype of the two top seeds facing off set in. In any case, it was the last MLB games we’ll see for at least six months, or possibly longer with the 2027 season fully up in the air due to the incoming lockout. So, what did you think of this year’s World Series? Did it live up to your expectations? Or were you a little disappointed?

item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 07: Head coach Micah Shrewsberry of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish looks on during the ACC basketball tip off at Hilton Charlotte Uptown on October 07, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Villanova Wildcats (0-0) vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish (0-0) Where : Palazzo dello Sport (Rome, Italy) When: Sunday, November 1 at 9:30 AM EST Betting Line: Villanova -7.5 (subject to change) How to Watch: FOX How to Listen : Villanova Sports Radio Network KenPom: Villanova 32, Notre Dame 83 Torvik: Villanova 30, Notre Dame 81 Evan Miya : Villanova 30, Notre Dame 83 About Notre Dame : Micah Shrewsberry, the former Penn State head coach, is going into his fourth season with Notre Dame. Shrewsberry took over for Mike Brey, who coached the team for the previous 23 years. Brey had this program nationally relevant more often than not throughout his tenure, but that has yet to be the case for Shrewsberry. In his final season with Penn State, Shrewsberry led the Nittany Lions to an NCAA-Tournament birth and a second round game against No. 2 Texas, coming up just short in a 71-66 loss. The expectations were that he would parlay that into success with Notre Dame, but through three seasons his combined record is 41-56. Things are not expected to go any better this year for the Fighting Irish, as they were picked to finish 16th in an 18-team ACC. Notre Dame had no players selected for preseason honors. The only two programs selected to finish behind the Fighting Irish were Boston College and Georgia Tech, both of whom have new coaches. Notre Dame played two exhibition games, both away from home. The first game came at Dayton, where Notre Dame fell 75-65. In the second contest, the Fighting Irish took down fellow Big East team DePaul 71-63. Notre Dame’s leading scorer in the Dayton game was Penn transfer Ethan Roberts, who Villanova fans should be familiar with over the past two seasons. Roberts averaged 16.9 points, three rebounds and 3.9 assists per game for the Quakers a year ago, and he projects as a potential leading scorer for Notre Dame this season. He was the only player in double-figures on the night with 11. In the contest with DePaul, starting center Logan Duncomb missed the game with a leg injury. Listed as day-to-day, the expectation is that the 6’10” senior will be available against Villanova. Duncomb is a senior transfer from Winthrop who averaged 18.3 points and 8.9 rebounds per game. The leading scorers in the game against the Blue Demons were Brady Koehler with 19, Braeden Smith with 17 and Jonathan Sanderson with 13. Koehler is a 6’10” sophomore who averaged 5.6 points per game in his freshman year for Notre Dame. He is a capable three-point shooter for his height, having made 4/10 in the exhibition games. Smith, a 6’ senior transfer from Gonzaga, averaged 5.1 points per game for the Bulldogs a year ago. Smith played his first two seasons at Colgate, averaging 11.6 and 12.

item.title: Siena basketball coach Nevada Smith treats student managers to dinner
item.description: Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith, front left, took the team's student managers out to dinner at Beer Bones Bar & Grill in Latham on Wednesday before the Saints open at Bryant next Monday. (Courtesy of Nevada Smith) LOUDONVILLE - It was a team outing of sorts, except without the players. New Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith took nine of his student managers to dinner on Wednesday at Beer Bones Bar & Grill in Latham. Only one manager on vacation was missing. "Just had some wings, got to watch some sports," senior Fen Egan of Mechanicville said. "Just connect and have a good time." It was Smith's way of saying thanks to the students who handle the behind-the-scenes tasks for the Saints, who open their season Monday against Bryant in Smithfield, R.I. "We do that at the beginning of the year, every year," Smith, a former Marquette assistant, said. "Just an appreciation for them so they understand how important they are to our organization. Everything they do helps us, helps every guy on our team. I think we have the best managing group in the country. I'd put them up against anyone. They're hard-working. They're intelligent. They understand what we're looking for." On a college basketball team, student managers handle everything from setting up equipment, to handing out towels and water bottles, to assisting in workouts. At the beginning of Thursday's practice, Egan, a former Mechancville guard, and other managers took part in halfcourt drills. "Same thing with the players, whatever it takes to win," Egan said. "Everybody's got a job and it's important that everybody does their job at the highest level possible." Siena has 10 student managers to assist the coaching staff and 16 players on the roster. The Saints listed four managers last season under former head coach Gerry McNamara. "We wouldn't bring someone in that wasn't a great fit for us," Smith said. "We wouldn't bring someone in who didn't bring value for our program. They all do such a great job with our guys. We live a lot in individual workouts and we need a lot of guys around the gym. They're a huge part of what we do and how we do it." Egan said every coach he's served under - Carmen Maciariello, McNamara and Smith - has treated the managers very well. "Every staff gives us a lot of opportunity," Egan said. "It's just a gift to be able to come and learn from them, and from the players, and just have that family relationship." Coyle gaining strength Smith said he thinks graduate forward Brendan Coyle of Niskayuna will be available for Monday's opener. Coyle missed the Oct. 18 exhibition loss to Syracuse with an upper-body injury. Coyle was dressed and participating at the start of Thursday's practice. "He's starting to come back full strength," Smith said. "We're excited to see where we can be when he's at full strength. We really haven't had that yet. He's a guy that we look to to calm us down, make some plays, that understands what winning at the highest level looks like

item.title: They played for Celtic – Peter Wilson
item.description: They played for Celtic – Peter Wilson Ayrshire born Peter Wilson signed for Celtic in May 1923 from hometown side Beith, and would go on to represent the hoops for eleven years as well as winning four caps for Scotland… Peter Wilson Celtic FC. Image by Celtic Curio for Celtic in the Thirties by Matt Corr The talented right half would make his debut on 16th February 1924 in a 1-0 league win over Motherwell at Fir Park. His job that day was to mark the Steelmen’s talented winger Bob Ferrier, one of the best and most feared players of his day in the Scottish game, yet Peter Wilson equipped himself well as he helped Celtic to a much deserved victory and also a clean sheet. Peter was an exceptional passer of the ball, and had a terrific footballing brain, he was always one step ahead in his thinking as he set up attacks for the Hoops over his time at Celtic. Peter Wilson, Celtic FC. Photo The Celtic Wiki It was once said of the Celtic right-half: “Peter Wilson didn’t pass the ball, he stroked it“. He was certainly heralded as a very fine player, and was said to have a “cool style“, “easy-oasy“, and was a “carpet artist”. Unfortunately for Peter, Rangers were the dominant side in that era, and he would win just one solitary league winners medal, although his luck in the Scottish Cup was much better as he picked up four winners medals (1925, 1927, 1931 and 1933). Peter Wilson, Celtic FC. Photo The Celtic Wiki It was something of a bleak era for the club, but Peter was one of the players exempt from criticism, a testament to the ability he possessed, with the league title winning season 1925/26 regarded as his most productive campaign, with the accomplished Jimmy McStay and John Mcfarlane beside him in the Celtic defence. Celtic 1930/31. Back; Willie Cook, Peter Kavanagh, Hugh Smith & Peter Wilson. Middle; Peter McGonagle, Chic Geatons, Denis O’Hare, John Thomson, Bobby Whitelaw, Willie Hughes & Will Quinn (Trainer). Front; Bertie Thomson, Alec Thomson, Jimmy McGrory, Jimmy McStay, Peter Scarff & Charlie Napier. Photo Celtic in the Thirties by Matt Corr After making 395 appearances and scoring 15 goals in an 11 year career in the famous green and white hoops, Peter would leave the club and sign for the Ggreen and white of Hibernian in the summer of 1934. Peter perhaps didn’t achieve the recognition that some of his more ‘popular’ teammates such as Patsy Gallagher, Tommy McInally, and Jimmy McGrory received, but he was very much a valued member of the Celtic side of that particular era. item.title: How Injuries Hit Pro Marathoners in the Wallet
item.description: About two and a half weeks before she was due to line up at Sunday’s New York City Marathon, elite runner Fiona O’Keeffe had to share a change of plans . Instead of racing through the five boroughs on Sunday, she’d be recovering from surgery to repair a fully retracted tendon tear in her hamstring. Though they work hard to stay healthy, injury is a fact of life for elite marathoners, who often log upward of 100 miles weekly. “A lot of these folks, they’re dealing with something at all times,” Dr. Efren Caballes, a sports medicine physician in Colorado who treats both professional and recreational endurance athletes, tells Front Office Sports . “It’s just a matter of, how often does it start to limit their training?” These setbacks are physically and emotionally challenging for any elite athlete. For professional marathoners, they can also be expensive. O’Keeffe placed fourth and set the American course record of 2:22:49 in NYC last year, earning $50,000 in prize money . Withdrawing means she misses her chance to compete for her share of this year’s $969,000 purse . And athletes who don’t make it to the starting line typically forfeit all the appearance fees offered by World Marathon Majors and other big races, agent Hawi Keflezighi tells FOS. (He doesn’t represent O’Keeffe, but has several clients in Sunday’s race, including Zouhair Talbi and Annie Frisbie. Appearance deals are individually negotiated and typically confidential.) In 2025, pro runner Lindsay Flanagan had to scratch from three marathons she’d committed to: Boston, Chicago, and Valencia. The money she lost in appearance fees would have at least doubled her income from her base contract and coaching, and if she’d performed well, she could have earned even more in prize money and bonuses. “We don’t do it for the money, but at the same time, this is how I pay my mortgage,” she tells FOS . “It’s my job. I think it would be crazy if I wasn’t upset about that.” The Cost of Care To add to the strain, many pro runners bear the brunt of their own healthcare costs. Professional sports leagues like the NFL, NBA, and WNBA have collective bargaining agreements governing areas like pay, working conditions, and healthcare coverage. Pro runners, meanwhile, operate as independent contractors without such protections, agent Josh Cox tells FOS . Runners’ primary sponsorships typically come from footwear companies, and with rare exceptions, these deals don’t include health insurance, Cox says. Some brands include a line item in contracts to cover premiums, Keflezighi says, while others have team setups that offer support. For example, a training group might have a physical therapist or other health professional on staff, or offer access to other recommended providers, with some or all costs paid for out of a team budget. item.title: NFL Predictions: Can the Bears’ defense slow down the Seahawks’ offense?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks is tackled by safety Jonathan Owens #36 of the Chicago Bears during the third quarter of an NFL football game, at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A Monday Night Football matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks is a circle-the-calendar game that NFL fans got excited about on schedule release day. Those games don’t always feel quite as big once the season gets rolling, but this one gets the full court press of hype (even more so with each team making a big-time trade). The (5-2) Bears are coming off a prime-time win over the New England Patriots, and the (4-3) Seahawks are coming off a prime-time win over the Kansas City Chiefs. These are two legit Super Bowl contenders. Ben Johnson’s Bears have one of the NFL’s most explosive offenses, and Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks again have one of the league’s most suffocating defenses, but this game might come down to the other side of the ball. Can Chicago’s defense slow down a Seahawks offense with a refocused rushing attack and one of the game’s best wide receivers, Jaxon Smith-Njigba? item.title: Arizona men’s tennis: Clancy Shields committed for the long haul after breakthrough season
item.description: For the better part of a decade, Arizona men’s tennis was knocking on the door of college tennis’ version of the promised land, the NCAA Championships. This spring, Clancy Shields ’ program broke through by advancing to the NCAA quarterfinals for the first time in history. The achievement affirmed Arizona’s status as one of the sport’s rising programs. The experience also affirmed Shields’ desire to stay in Tucson and build out a program he thinks can compete with anyone nationally. Shields, who is entering his 11th year as Arizona’s head coach, signed a contract in August that runs through the 2030-31 season. The announcement may have gone under the radar, but it was one of the biggest moves athletic director Desiree Reed-Francois made during the offseason. Not that Reed-Francois needed to do a lot of selling. “I told Desiree, ‘I want always to be — if I can and if you guys are willing to do it — I want to have a contract that the players who end up coming here feel like I’m going to be here and that there’s stability,’” Shields said last month. “If you come to play for Arizona you’re going to come play for me for the entirety of your career.” Shields’ decision to staying in one place comes off as refreshing in an era where coaches and players are all too often willing to jump at the highest-paying suitor, even when they’ve got a good thing going where they are. Shields has no doubt had chances to look elsewhere after taking over a program with a lackluster history and turning it into one of the best programs in the Western states. Shields’ program is coming off a fifth consecutive conference championship. The Wildcats concluded 2026 with a No. 7 ranking, the highest final ranking in program history. And for the second year in a row, Arizona produced an All-American standout — first Colton Smith followed by Jay Friend . “The grass isn’t always greener somewhere else,” Shields said. “As much as people will try to come poach you or say ‘Hey, come to this place, you can do things here,’ I always say that with (players), If you’re looking to get in the portal or doing this, we’ve all had the opportunity to look around and do things. “This is what makes this place special is that we’ve all committed to being here and to grow this place, to grow this program and the culture that we’ve built.” Shields’ philosophy defies the transactional culture that defines much of college athletics. item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The New York Mets claimed Los Angeles Angels infielder Kyren Paris off of waivers Thursday, ending his seven-year stint in the organization. The Angels drafted Paris in the second round of the 2019 draft, and he featured in parts of four seasons for the team in MLB. INF Kyren Paris has been claimed off waivers by the New York Mets — Angels PR (@LAAngelsPR) October 29, 2026 Paris played in eight hames for the Angels in 2026, striking out eight times in 15 hitless at-bats while walking three times. He saw his longest run of MLB action in 2025, when he had. blistering start to the season after breaking camp with the team. Paris had an OPS higher than 1.000 through the middle of April in 2025 before falling into a slump and returning to Triple-A. Through his 88 games in MLB from 2023-26, Paris had seven homers and 17 RBIs, posting a .510 OPS with 101 strikeouts in 232 at-bats. Paris featured in both Double-A and Triple-A this season, posting a .842 OPS in 93 games, though he had a .981 OPS in Triple-A. The Angels didn’t have an explicit need for Paris in their team, as their outfield consisted of players better than him for the majority of the season. Mike Trout obviously commanded a spot in the outfield for the entire season, and Wade Meckler also made himself at home with some strong performances throughout the year. Factoring in Christian Moore’s transition to outfield and the contributions of players like Jose Siri, Josh Lowe and Bryce Teodosio, there wasn’t much room for Paris. item.title: Cowboys have chance they can’t let fly away against Cardinals
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose games they’re supposed to win, having already dropped such games to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants. The Cowboys suffered their fifth loss of the 2025 season to the Cardinals in week nine at home last year, and now are looking to avoid the same amount of losses through week seven against the same opponent – one they haven’t beaten since 2017, even with three of the four meetings since that win in Arizona coming in Arlington. If not for that 28-17 Cowboys win in 2017, the Cardinals would actually have an active nine-game winning streak against the Cowboys coming into this weekend, with the last win before that one coming in 2006. The 2-5 Cardinals opened their season with what felt like an upset win at the time at the Chargers, who remain winless. In week six, they went back to SoFi Stadium and scored a legitimate upset against a division rival, beating the Rams 18-16. This snapped a four-game losing streak to the Seahawks, 49ers, Giants, and Lions, but Mike LaFleur’s team also could not stack wins as they lost last Sunday at home to the Broncos. Let’s get to our weekly look at what the Cowboys must do to finally get the monkey cardinal off their back and beat these pesky red birds, or what could throw the season back off the rails with another bad home loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Arizona Cardinals if… …they set the edge on defense. There was one thing the Cowboys still struggled to do for the majority of the Philadelphia Eagles game. While the offense got points early and kept the pressure on most of the night, and the defense avoided the backbreaking plays and penalties until that offense handed them a sizeable lead, and the kicking game swung the field position battle in Dallas’ favor, still, the defense had a hard time setting the edge. If ever the stage was set for a game to help prove the Cowboys are different this year, Sunday afternoon is the ultimate “do-over” game, because the defense couldn’t set an edge at all against Jacoby Brissett and these Cardinals under Matt Eberflus in 2025. A strong run game on the edge, missed tackles, and the dual-threat ability of Brissett also gave the Cowboys defense no chance to hold up in coverage, as Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride caught touchdowns – the latter making the score 24-7 in the third quarter. Christian Parker’s Cowboys defense showed new looks in the middle of the field against the Eagles with Shemar James and Demarvion Overshown at linebacker. The personnel elsewhere in the secondary is also better than when these teams met last season when Markquese Bell, Juanyeh Thomas, and Kaiir Elam all started.

item.title: A Camden Chat Thanks, and Farewell
item.description: Dear Camden Chatters, today is my last day as a writer for this blog. I’ve been writing here since the 2019 season, though I was a fan way before that. I definitely won’t stop being a fan of this site, but I’m hanging up my cleats as a writer today. I want to say thanks. Back in 2014, when Adam Jones circled Oriole Park carrying the AL East Champions flag after the team clinched, then pied a bunch of people in the face, I felt a real urge to share the joy somewhere. Same, too, with the Delmon Young double—could you believe how noisy the stadium was? Same, a few years later, when John Means pitched a no-hitter. And when the O’s won the division title in 2023 and Gunnar Henderson was named Rookie of the Year. And many others. Those moments are special because you have people to share them with, like this community. I loved being a part of it as a writer. Now, I won’t deny that I wasn’t always a good writer. There have been some very bad takes on my part in seven years. I thought utility superman Stevie Wilkerson should get regular playing time. I believed in the Shintaro Fujinami reclamation project . I got on the Spenser Watkins bandwagon, if such a thing even existed. There were times it was hard to write, because the on-field product sucked. I did a whole piece on whether the 2021 Orioles, who finished 52-110, were the worst O’s team in history. (They have a strong claim. Maikel Franco played a bunch, we tried to fix Matt Harvey, and Pat Valaika was an infield fixture. Blech.) The team never did win a single playoff game while I was a writer here. I’ve been frustrated by some of the recent changes I’ve seen. I hope the term “ liftoff ” is soon forgotten, because if it’s remembered, I think it will be ironically, meaning the Orioles will continue to be bad. I wish Heston Kjerstad had panned out. I wish the team hadn’t traded Trey Mancini, or Ramón Urías, and especially not Adley Rutschman this year, I don’t care what the return was. item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May Dustin May was traded from the St. Louis Cardinals to the Milwaukee Brewers this season, but now he will be looking for a new contract. item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 19: Ben Davies of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates after scoring their third goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 19, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ben Davies isn’t planning on retiring anytime soon, but he’s already starting to think about what comes next in his career. A fan favorite and currently the longest-tenured player at Tottenham Hotspur, Davies is beloved at Spurs and deeply respected by the club and every manager that has come and gone over the last decade when he’s been at the club. But Davies is 33 now, the Wales national team captain, and understands that all things must come to an end eventually. In an interview with the BBC, Davies says that while he hopes to keep playing football for a few more years, he’s looking at what happens after he hangs up his boots — and that he’d be interested in both a coaching role, or even a move to the boardroom of a football club. “Look, hopefully [retirement] is still quite a few years away. I feel fit. I love playing football, and I want to play as long as I can. But you’re a long time retired in this game, and I don’t see myself just doing nothing after football. “For me, it’s a great learning experience as well – to see how it all works behind the scenes in the world of football. This is a great start. It’s more than just a role for me; it’s great to be able to give back as much as I can to a footballing country that’s given me so much. “It’s hard to put a nail in it where your future lies. If something falls on my lap in the coaching world, then maybe that will be my route. But I want to be able to use my expertise and what I’ve learned in the best way that it can be, and I don’t know what angle that takes after football yet. “I’d like to be someone who maybe, at some point, crosses that divide from a player to the boardroom or a front-office kind of role, because I haven’t seen too many players over the years who have done that. “I think it definitely adds a pretty good perspective when making decisions.” I think we all expected Davies to move into coaching after his playing days are done.
